findings.title: Native CLI acceptance tests still require the pre-v2.2.0 terminal lifecycle and unauthenticated Cloud dispatch
findings.scenario: Run the existing guardian-native acceptance cases against the pinned native fixture. The hooks case successfully closes a proven-clean CLI tree and then asserts unknown:true/activity_unknown. The Cloud case creates a fresh zero-credential fixture, expects terminal/open(codex-cloud) to dispatch and emit Not signed in, and then expects the same unknown state.
findings.actual: Confirmed CLI cleanup now sets restarting:true and raises runtime_restarting without making activity unknown. Cloud open checks account/read and throws chatgpt_login_required before process/spawn for this unauthenticated fixture.
findings.impact: These two existing acceptance cases contradict the implemented and unit-tested behavior and prevent a passing full validation run. This is a test regression, not evidence that the intended production automatic-refresh behavior is defective.
findings.evidence: Static executable-call-chain proof: CliTerminals.finish invokes host.settled; RuntimeService.settled sets restarting; RuntimeService.admit rejects with runtime_restarting. The fixture uses a newly created empty CODEX_HOME with a local requires_openai_auth=false provider and no ChatGPT credential, so the Cloud precheck rejects before its expected terminal output.
findings.verification: No native acceptance run performed during read-only audit; assertions and implementation are directly contradictory.
findings.recommendation: Update both native acceptance cases to verify the current automatic-refresh and pre-dispatch ChatGPT-login contract while retaining the isolated fixture and no-external-network checks.

findings.title: Runtime verification guide still describes proven CLI cleanup as unknown with explicit durable restart
findings.scenario: A maintainer follows the current terminal/open lifecycle description or uses it to assess the expected CLI exit acceptance result.
findings.actual: The guide says proven cleanup marks the runtime unknown and requires explicit durable restart. RuntimeService now marks restarting, emits restart-required and the worker/entrypoint schedules an automatic refresh; unknown is reserved for failed cleanup.
findings.impact: The current contract documentation directs maintainers toward the obsolete state and manual recovery expectation and aligns with the stale native tests above.
findings.evidence: tests/runtime/README.md:106 versus src/runtime/service.ts:130-136 and tests/runtime/cli-terminals.test.ts:98-104; worker restart response/drain lifecycle was read in src/runtime/main.ts and tests/runtime/server.test.ts.
findings.recommendation: Update the current lifecycle description to automatic refresh after proven cleanup, preserving separately identified historical acceptance evidence.

additionalCrossDomainReview.candidate: Fresh install lacks runtime.json, so explicit default-provider model/list could invoke catalog-server and fail.
additionalCrossDomainReview.disposition: Not confirmed; the proposed call path is blocked by an intentional legacy fallback.
additionalCrossDomainReview.evidence: install_recovery.py:317-329 creates a legacy single-provider generation and provider.env without HARNESS_PROVIDER_REGISTRY_FILE. main.ts:132-138 leaves RuntimeConfig.providerRegistry absent. ManagedProviders.list at providers.ts:73-77 then strips explicit modelProvider and calls the existing main native account/read and model/list. It does not invoke providerCatalog/catalog-server, whose runtime.json read is in native_launcher.py:256-263.

limitations: This report covers all assigned source and test files by static review. It is not a claim of full-repository review, full test execution, live-account acceptance or production readiness. No additional production-runtime defect was confirmed within this scope.
